correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed both operator inclusions rather than just the rank count. Each simple cycle of a cactus is a cycle block. The vertex/cycle-block incidence bipartite graph is a forest, giving independent F2 incidence relations; any nonempty relation sum has at least two nonzero coordinates, so quotient vectors are nonloops and dimension is |V|-k. Every cycle-infection is a linear dependence and hence belongs to quotient-span closure. Conversely, for a closed infection set H and quotient-dependent w outside H, choose a forest of cycle relations with symmetric difference supported in H union {w}; pruning a farthest cycle block from w forces its parent into H, removes that cycle without losing the witness at w, and eventually forces w, contradiction. Independence definitions give both directions for Helly and Radon sizes in a loopless represented matroid. Independently generated 130 distinct random small cactus cases and exhaustively compared hulls versus F2 quotient span on 146,432 subsets, not treating those finite cases as universal proof.

This addresses a motivated structural tractability gap beyond separately known forest or one-cycle ranks. final_claim: For every connected simple finite cactus graph with at least three vertices, the entire cycle-infection convex hull operator agrees with the closure of a loopless binary representable matroid F2^V/span{cycle incidence vectors}. Its Helly, Radon and convex-independence rank parameters each equal |V|-k=2|V|-|E|-1, where k is the number of cycle blocks.
limitations: Only connected simple cacti with at least three vertices, and the stated Helly/Radon definitions.
No proof for arbitrary cycle-overlapping graphs or all matroidal convexity classes.
